summary: The synthetic geometry does not force acceptance.
rationale: The module supplies both valid and invalid states. The consumer runs all of them through evaluateLayout and asserts explicit failure reasons, so copied probe coordinates are test inputs rather than a PASS override.

summary: The screenshot judge fails closed.
rationale: Every missing credential, fetch failure, non-OK response, and non-verdict path returns pass:false. Current head only removes the lead comment and does not weaken the behavior.

summary: Reachable layout verification fails closed.
rationale: exitCode permits GAP, but no verifier producer emits GAP. Missing specs, screenshots, judges, and controls become FAIL.

summary: Trip-site HTTP failures other than 404 can still produce onboarding PASS.
rationale: Require a successful final HTTP status, add 3xx/403/429/5xx cases, and prove no packet can pass with them.

summary: Provisioning is fail-closed.
rationale: Missing credentials, missing minted rows, and missing chat URLs throw. verify-layout records the provisioning exception as FAIL rather than skipping or passing the four-state check.

summary: The doctor fails closed on readiness, page, viewport, and build-stamp errors.
rationale: Caught fetch/browser errors append reasons. Non-200 version responses, page status at least 400, absent stamps, and mismatches all make ok false.

summary: Provisioning helper cannot manufacture a verdict.
rationale: Direct execution prints instructions; the imported mint function owns state creation.

summary: The active state classifier uses API vacation counts rather than dropdown-option fixture counts.
rationale: Snapshot fetch failures remain non-OK, a missing composer yields no state, and the deprecated DOM-only stateId has no acceptance caller. The helpers do not force a passing verdict.

summary: The shared-trip and signup drivers fail closed on real browser outcomes.
rationale: The module does not synthesize a successful layout row. Navigation, missing coupon reachability, hydration, and screenshot errors reach finishRow as failures, and verify-layout consumes those rows in its final exit status.

summary: Measured and judged layout failures reach the command exit status.
rationale: Unreachable prerequisites produce pass:false rows, finishRow requires measurement and judge success, and main exits nonzero when any row fails. The audit-head diff removes comments only.

summary: The welcome verifier fails closed on incomplete capture or an absent judge pass.
rationale: Owner, collaborator, and no-vacation capture errors become missing or failed precheck evidence. buildJudgePacket derives its result from onboardingVerdict, which requires both the precheck and an explicit external judge pass. The returned ok flag is true only when packet.pass is true.

summary: Closed TSV #322 explicitly owns the still-self-referential Budget completeness checks.
rationale: Do not create duplicate ownership. Reopen or explicitly supersede TSV #322 before changing the independent Budget acceptance expectations.

summary: PR336 can render an unassigned flight on every itinerary day.
rationale: Require a flight assignment or explicit matching dayIds before adding an unassigned flight. Add a negative test for a timeline flight with no assignment and no dayIds. Route all displayed day headings through one helper so titled days still include the required day number.

summary: The detail model omits absent or incomplete fields instead of fabricating values.
rationale: The catch in safeHttpUrl converts invalid external input to a non-link, not PASS. ThingDetailPanel renders only the returned rows, reviews, and URLs; no comment text participates in acceptance.

summary: Media helpers filter placeholders and expose actual stored media.
rationale: The helpers do not invent successful media rows. Saved-story and print rendering depend on real bound media, explicit flags, and non-junk URLs.

summary: Keepsake sections derive from shared-trip records and explicit print flags.
rationale: Empty summaries, stories, maps, and directories stay absent. Query flags can disable configured sections but do not synthesize content or convert missing data into acceptance.

summary: PR336 summary padding is already owned by #402.
rationale: Do not duplicate the established PR336 summary-padding finding.

summary: The source implementation measures the rendered glyph rather than returning an acceptance verdict.
rationale: TabEmojiIcon repaints on layout and resize. The PR336 theater-mask adjustment changes product pixels but does not alter a gate, fixture result, or pass threshold, so it is not a false-pass special case.

summary: Tab visibility and URL selection do not synthesize acceptance.
rationale: The module maps trip configuration and permissions into navigation state and has no gate-pass path. The audit-head includes-to-some rewrite is behaviorally equivalent for membership checking.

summary: The head deletion does not change effective Vite typing.
rationale: The source file contains only the Vite type reference. Head empties it, but tsconfig already includes vite/client explicitly, so no runtime or acceptance behavior changes.

summary: The declarative detail fixture does not itself create a false pass; NYC layout ownership remains with TSV #408.
rationale: Do not duplicate the existing LAYOUT-NYC audit. This fixture adds no separate bypass.

summary: The normal CI test command silently skips every browser layout acceptance suite.
rationale: Make the CI quality-gate job provide a browser switch and execute shell-layout, or fail when layout acceptance is unavailable. Do not treat the current skip as a successful full test run.

summary: The source mega-comment made route-wiring regex assertions pass without proving the symbols were executable in this module.
rationale: Do not open duplicate follow-through. The current branch removes the false proof and verifies executable owners.

summary: New-rule seed rows need not match current findings, pre-authorizing arbitrary future suppressions.
rationale: Require every new-rule seed row to correspond to a current finding and fail or prune unmatched stale entries. Add a regression where an unused future path or symbol under a new rule cannot pre-authorize a later suppression.

summary: Build attribution rejects unexplained or reply-affecting drift.
rationale: Mismatch needs a nonempty ancestry list and every path must be evidence or explicitly allowlisted. Missing metadata, reply changes, non-ancestry, and inconsistent transcript SHAs throw.

summary: The hard-coded NYC capture path is reserved to #408.
rationale: Do not duplicate the superseding LAYOUT-NYC finding formerly associated with #404.

summary: The script is a bounded manual capture, not an acceptance gate.
rationale: It can emit no image when pills are absent and mixes historical JS with repository fixture and styling. No caller consumes these images as PASS evidence, so it cannot turn a product or gate failure into acceptance.

summary: The image stand-in is symmetric capture data, not acceptance.
rationale: Both sides receive the same bytes. Missing tabs/content throw, and the CLI has no PASS return path.

summary: The code ratchet names the vacation-client source root but silently rejects every nested app path.
rationale: Make inScope recognize every configured root and add an app source violation that must appear in the ratchet report. Keep baseline seed-row authorization under the baseline-subset follow-through.

summary: The checker exemptions are narrow and acceptance remains fail-closed.
rationale: Paid-host exemptions apply only to exact checker ban-list rows. API dates require a matching header and entire literal value. BUNDLE-LEAK recursively scans raw upstream content, and padding uses an always-fail identity that a baseline cannot suppress.

summary: The diagnostic validates persisted EULA records and exits nonzero on missing evidence.
rationale: It does not grant staging acceptance or replace a failed read with fixture data. The exact receipt key and session hashes must validate against database records.

summary: The exporter reports count validation without claiming an import occurred.
rationale: It writes a dry-run bundle and report, and its status derives from explicit source-to-export count equality. No downstream deployment or acceptance consumer was found.

summary: PR336 changes acceptance to the synthetic positive NYC fixture.
rationale: The contract explicitly preserves those existing owners and forbids duplicate findings.

summary: Declarative scanner fixture has explicit controls.
rationale: It is read as text and never enters product data or a gate verdict.

summary: The Nominatim doubles preserve the production throttle and cache boundaries used by their tests.
rationale: The faithful executor recognizes the same UPDATE RETURNING, cache upsert, and cache select operations as the production store. Dedicated tests exercise throttle waits, cache hits, expiry, aliases, and failures. The simpler memory store is explicitly selected only by tests that do not claim Neon SQL parity.

summary: Hardcoded NYC values are scoped fixture facts.
rationale: Consumers are fixture/capture/contract checks; provenance-blocked fields are cleared before finalization.

summary: Recorded bad rows are adversarial inputs, not approved results.
rationale: Callers mix off-target and on-target candidates, run production relevance logic, and assert the recorded Senegal and non-Kaanapali rows are excluded.

summary: The Hertz fixture exercises provider parsing and persistence instead of bypassing them.
rationale: Tests pass the recorded row through Brave display-title, rental-category, place-row, persistence, and shared-trip paths. The empty categories field is an input under test rather than a prefilled expected category.

summary: The duplicate fixture covers a real provider-shape conflict and does not precompute the parser result.
rationale: The consumer combines both rows and verifies title selection and same-URL provider-rank deduplication. Neither fixture carries a pass marker or fixture-specific branch key.

summary: The Maui constants are test-provider inputs, not production fixture selection.
rationale: Callers inject the records through mock fetch paths and still execute search ranking, radius, and rejection code. No product branch detects these values or hard-codes PASS.

summary: The OSM constants are provider input, not a precomputed PASS.
rationale: The consumer runs the payload through the OSM parser and production save/reply flow. The fixture exports no verdict or acceptance override.

summary: Event-logo fixture scope is derived from the shared PR336 registry.
rationale: The module neither invents rows nor treats absent recordings as success. Its IDs constrain fetch and replay flows, which retain explicit blocked evidence for unresolved targets.

summary: The xAI registry identifies capture work but does not grant acceptance.
rationale: Consumers still require matching recordings and keys. Missing captures fail their builders. PR336 candidate keeps this module unchanged.

summary: Closed TSV #355 explicitly preserves row 608 as failing while acceptance filters it out.
rationale: Do not duplicate ownership. Reopen or supersede TSV #355 if row 608 is required for PR336 acceptance; until then, report the filtered failure and withhold full data-contract approval.

summary: The LAYOUT-NYC path depends on a hard-coded local NYC screenshot seed.
rationale: #408 supersedes #404 and owns the LAYOUT-NYC hard-coded reference data and acceptance path.

summary: The Hyatt record supplies test input and expected extraction but does not bypass the classifier or route gates.
rationale: Its callers separately exercise tripIntakeJobFields, prompt construction, saved-title handling, and live-path persistence. The fixture has no pass field or product runtime hook.

summary: The fixture asserts classifier outputs without bypassing classification.
rationale: Expected values are compared to actual classifier results. The rows do not flow into runtime acceptance or manufacture a PASS response.

summary: The mock fixture checks transformations but does not approve staging behavior.
rationale: Its canned payloads remain inside an offline contract test. Assertions verify parsed ratings, reviews, source links, and model provenance, and no production or Gate B return path consumes the fixture result.

summary: The harness serves committed application artifacts and state-specific API data; it does not return test verdicts.
rationale: The consumer performs DOM geometry, hit testing, controls, overflow, full-screen, and send behavior checks and exits nonzero on any missing result. Generic /api fixture responses do not decide those layout assertions.

summary: The 30-word threshold can accept PR336's generic summary padding.
rationale: Do not duplicate the established summary-quality threshold finding.

summary: The logo comparator can pass candidates that violate both declared centering thresholds.
rationale: Require every candidate to meet an explicit absolute or bounded-reference contract, fail unmatched expected rows, and include the Stores logoCenter pass in the aggregate gate.

summary: The logo centering gate measures a newly centered redraw, not the browser's rendered logo position.
rationale: Replace the synthetic redraw metric with pixels captured from the actual rendered wrapper, or compute the real img rect and intrinsic ink offset in wrapper coordinates. Add a negative regression that deliberately offsets the img and must fail while the centered case passes. Keep screenshots as evidence, not an unexamined side artifact.

summary: The LOGO ink gate measures styled chip chrome instead of isolating logo pixels.
rationale: Measure only image or fallback glyph pixels, or mask chip border/background. Add a production-styled blank or transparent image regression that requires row and Cars logo gates to fail.

summary: Recorded event-logo enrichment preserves evidence rather than synthesizing success.
rationale: Only committed responses keyed to a target query are replayed. Missing matches remain in blocked/source diagnostics, and stale logo fields are removed before enrichment.

summary: Source reversibly encodes the banned model ID.
rationale: Current branch already has the scoped fix and regression.

summary: Icon centering is measured from rendered pixels and fails outside tolerance.
rationale: The helper derives ink centers from screenshots rather than DOM claims. Its primary test proves the old bundle fails and the fixed bundle passes, while shell layout asserts each tab row exists.

summary: The event-logo source check exercises enrichment and rejects unrelated or reused logos.
rationale: Gate B event rows must have a nonempty, unique logo, Tavily source evidence, a matching website host, and no blocked marker. Negative cases prove mismatched and shared logos fail. The assertions consume recorded PR336 sources rather than injecting pass booleans.

summary: Invalid timing evidence is rewritten into valid-looking evidence.
rationale: Reject zev= and any timing line missing an original jev= token before rendering. Remove the replacement. Change the poisoned-input regression to require nonzero exit and no PDF output.

summary: Provider helpers only shape model requests.
rationale: They return no verdict. Non-tier-1 calls receive no override, and missing model configuration fails at the API boundary.

summary: The wrapper does not contain an acceptance or bypass path.
rationale: It directly loads the local environment and replaces itself with the one-shot worker process. Shell strict mode propagates setup and worker failures.

summary: Direct coverage markers can convert a missing or rejected screenshot into captured coverage.
rationale: Make screenshot acceptance page-derived. Remove direct mark calls or record non-screen checks separately. Add captured coverage only after shot returns true and its page exists. Before writing VERIFY or the PDF, assert every captured feature has a corresponding page or an explicit exempt gap. Add a regression test for rejected and missing screenshots.

summary: The renderer embeds the image files selected by its caller and does not substitute screenshots.
rationale: build opens every page.image path with ImageReader and uses that file dimensions and bytes in the PDF. The one-pixel image is confined to the renderer unit test. The production caller supplies its capture manifest and fails if Python returns nonzero.

summary: ASK smoke checks require fresh-session, persisted, and provider-backed evidence.
rationale: Neither local comments nor canned response text satisfy the check. Missing session setup, HTTP success, persisted rows, Jev grade, or expected question behavior yields failure.

summary: Browser pooling bounds concurrency without swallowing failures.
rationale: Callback errors propagate after cleanup. The narrow connection retry rethrows after bounded attempts, and selector false is consumed as missing evidence rather than PASS.

summary: Check I requires the actual trip title and concrete outbound evidence.
rationale: The check cannot pass from a canned title. It resolves the persisted trip when state lacks a title and conjunctively requires status, exactly one outbound, evaluation, owner, link, and subject match.

summary: Composer reconciliation requires independent structural and pixel evidence.
rationale: It can change only the send-control rubric item after the live DOM proves an enabled visible button and the crop proves ink in its bounding box. Other failed rubric items remain failed.

summary: Composer acceptance reads live DOM visibility and hit-test facts and only records failures.
rationale: Missing composer, Send, attach, or voice controls fail. A hidden, covered, disabled, off-viewport, zero-size, or unexpected control also fails. No default-true or catch-and-pass branch exists.

summary: Stub and live modes have separate evidence contracts.
rationale: Staging stub requires status=stubbed/provider=harness_stub plus link, owner, title, and count checks. Live mode requires sent/resend/no error. Spec forbids the flag in launch/customer environments.

summary: EULA readback passes only on exact persisted receipt and session validation.
rationale: The module does not list for a nearby fixture or accept missing content. It requires exact object keys, valid hashes and fields, and zero blob-list calls.

summary: Reachable graders require rows and observed evidence.
rationale: Logo flow combines nonempty DOM chips, API URLs, two viewports, ink, and brand COM. Missing coffee/lodging evidence does not pass.

summary: Missing server timing disables the check-5 10-second threshold.
rationale: Make missing required trip-create timing a harness failure and add an absent-timing regression.

summary: Jev checks fail closed when the judge is absent, malformed, or negative.
rationale: Missing keys/credentials, invalid JSON, failed HTTP, exceptions, and null yes/no all return pass false.

summary: The generic DOM evaluator derives pass only from an empty failure list.
rationale: Missing required controls/messages and all geometry violations push failures. Separate LAYOUT-NYC infra behavior is owned by #408 and not duplicated here.

summary: The shared-header probe is part of the owned LAYOUT-NYC acceptance path.
rationale: #408 owns the header-probe and visual-reconciliation contract as one LAYOUT-NYC flow.

summary: LAYOUT-NYC suppresses judge failures and can end as non-failing INFRA_BLOCKED.
rationale: #408 supersedes #404 and owns this exact LAYOUT-NYC acceptance path, including current-head follow-through.

summary: The probe excludes content intentionally contained by clipping or scrolling ancestors but still fails page-level and visible overflow.
rationale: evaluateLayoutRules separately compares documentElement.scrollWidth to the viewport, then fails on any sampled unclipped descendant. The fixture tests cover clipped and unclipped cases; no exception names a product fixture or forces PASS.

summary: Timing guard is not used to prove publication.
rationale: The spine separately rejects non-200 preparation and the probe rejects hydration failure.

summary: The layout spine maps LAYOUT-NYC infrastructure failure to a non-failing smoke status.
rationale: #408 owns the end-to-end LAYOUT-NYC status mapping, so this audit records ownership without a duplicate issue.

summary: The proof runner can grade a deployment identified only by a seven-character SHA prefix.
rationale: Require exactly 40 hex characters and exact endpoint equality. Omit or mark unobserved deployment ID. Add negative tests for short input, same-prefix mismatch, and missing deployment ID.

summary: Visual-spine setup does not pass when preflight or infrastructure fails.
rationale: Failed browser registration and failed preflight return false or INFRA_BLOCKED. No catch converts those errors into an accepted layout result.

summary: Offline replay depends on persisted IDs and raw evidence.
rationale: D attribution requires request or response linkage, and A2 requires welcome_for plus transcript agreement. Missing or ambiguous evidence yields false/unmatched, not synthesized success.

summary: The logo-only staging runner propagates the live LOGO verdict to its process status.
rationale: The runner checks the deployed SHA, obtains a real shared page and API payload, calls runSharedSiteLogoCheck, writes its detailed result, and exits 1 when logoResult.pass is false. Partial initialization is overwritten by the returned check and cannot produce success.

summary: The main smoke phase uses concrete HTTP, database, classifier, and provider evidence.
rationale: No unconditional pass, comment-satisfied assertion, or synthetic staging response was found in this orchestration module. Specialized LAYOUT-NYC behavior is recorded on its assigned modules and owned by #408.

summary: Map and budget grading uses rendered state and persisted targets.
rationale: MAP requires mounted engine state, valid coordinates, bounds, and no relevant console failure. Budget text is checked against __budgetTargets. The split budget-key issue is already owned by #403 and is not duplicated.

summary: Dedicated smoke failures remain non-PASS.
rationale: The one retry is limited to browser connection closure. False results, exhausted retries, timeouts, and exceptions are recorded by the shared smoke runner rather than converted to success.

summary: Poll completion requires places and enough rows to exercise sorting.
rationale: Empty arrays and one-row tabs remain false. The helper does not fabricate seed rows or turn timeout/missing payload into readiness.

summary: The helper prevents syntax-invalid page evaluation without changing probe results.
rationale: It only packages an explicit expression into an IIFE and throws when the expression is absent. It does not supply a default pass value. LAYOUT-NYC ownership remains with #408.

summary: Parallelization does not weaken verdict aggregation.
rationale: The module only builds real check callbacks. The common runner records false returns, exceptions, timeouts, and infrastructure blocks as non-PASS outcomes.

summary: The plan correctly declares LAYOUT and VISUAL fail-closed.
rationale: Its declaration and disjointness checks are sound. The fail-open behavior is in createSmokeRunner.finish, reported against that assigned module.

summary: Any provider 429 becomes an explicit harness failure.
rationale: The extraction path preserves statuses and attachProviderLogAndMaybeFail returns pass:false on every detected 429. Final summaries are metrics and do not override the earlier failure.

summary: INFRA_BLOCKED GO checks can produce a passing GO gate and exit 0.
rationale: Require PASS for every GO entry. Missing, INFRA_BLOCKED, timed-out, or any non-PASS status must fail GO and exit nonzero while retaining diagnostics. Add blocked LAYOUT/VISUAL runner regressions.

summary: Hydration readiness does not by itself satisfy downstream shared-UI checks.
rationale: A DOM-ready shell can recover from a transient non-200 API response, but mapping and budget consumers still require concrete tabs, controls, places, and expected lines. Current audit head changes comments only.

summary: The smoke single-instance lock is not atomically acquired.
rationale: Create the lock with an exclusive atomic operation such as openSync using wx. Replace stale locks with a race-safe retry. Add a multi-process test that starts contenders together and proves exactly one acquires the lock.

summary: Tail checks preserve failure signals.
rationale: Fresh-session setup, callback errors, timeout outcomes, and false check results flow to the smoke recorder. The module contains no catch that returns a successful verdict after a failed check.

summary: The accurate DOM evidence feeds the known LAYOUT-NYC verdict suppression.
rationale: Keep this producer unchanged. Resolve downstream LAYOUT-NYC acceptance in #408 without duplicate ownership.

summary: The default-off sort prohibition is not the active LAYOUT-NYC acceptance mechanism.
rationale: Keep the LAYOUT-NYC investigation under TSV #408. This module supplies no separate false-pass finding.

summary: The aggregate grader closes the local under-two-row skip.
rationale: A single tab with fewer than two rows can be non-applicable, but gradeThingCardSortButtonsHarness requires at least one exercised multi-row case and successful priced-row sorting per viewport. Empty fixtures therefore cannot satisfy the aggregate contract.

summary: THING-CARD approval depends on live DOM, screenshot, row-ink, tag, and sort evidence.
rationale: The function does not accept a canned card or proof image as the staging result. Missing rows, failed detail interactions, tag mismatch, insufficient row ink, or aggregate sort failure propagates to the check result.

summary: The live harness records whether it used the repository UI spec or the explicit fallback.
rationale: At the audited source commit features/screens/app.md exists, so the fallback does not replace the governing file. Both layout and visual consumers receive the source label; no fallback value directly returns PASS.

summary: Every missing-key, metadata, HTTP, parse, timeout, and image response failure blocks VISUAL.
rationale: runVisualHarnessCheck returns pass false and infraBlocked before mint or judging unless visualPreflightReady sees both ok and imageOk. The test double does not alter the live fetch path.

summary: VISUAL ignores failed shared-tab seed posts and excludes their screenshots from its verdict.
rationale: Propagate the seed result into minting and fail VISUAL on any non-201 seed response. Add explicit shared-tab row assertions or include shared screenshots and hydration failures in the final pass predicate. Add a negative test with a failed seed post.

summary: The visual states are created through staging checkout, EULA, and app APIs rather than aliased to a known customer.
rationale: Each state uses a fresh coupon and session. The returned map contains URLs and ids but no pass field; capture and judge stages still determine acceptance.

summary: Visual acceptance requires real judged shots and all verdicts to pass.
rationale: The summary rejects an empty judged set and combines layout and visual-judge results. A skipped mint only supplies a pre-minted state map and does not manufacture a passing shot.

summary: Bundle stripping requires exact matches and verifies the final served artifact.
rationale: The rewriter does not replace removed callers with success stubs. Count mismatches and residual forbidden strings throw, and the production bundle loader runs the final assertion.

summary: The test static resolver rejects traversal and missing files.
rationale: Only regular files under the repository root or public directory resolve. The purchase-email test loudly asserts that the helper comes from public rather than treating a missing helper as success.

summary: ASK-d2 tests generated production prompts, not its comment.
rationale: It calls production context/request builders, requires the unscheduled fact, and scans both messages for nine solicitation forms.

summary: ASK-d2 asserts generated behavior and is manifest-wired.
rationale: It rejects lodging/day leakage and requires machine and plain not-on-a-day facts.

summary: This test exposes, but does not independently create, the baseline-subset bypass.
rationale: The suite has substantive behavior assertions for banned content and bundle provenance. Its five-row new-rule case is direct evidence for the new finding in baseline-subset.mjs, so reporting the same defect here would duplicate one underlying policy bug.

summary: The fixture exercises production grounding and rejects unsourced names.
rationale: The synthetic results establish a literal expected set, then production gates remove Hertz and Secret Taco while preserving a nonempty provider-grounded reply. Source-string checks are supplementary, not the acceptance result.

summary: The residual test asserts behavior through public flows.
rationale: Success cannot be satisfied by its comment. Literal assertions require a Brave row, persisted source ID, non-502 path, and wrong-island rejection.

summary: The test does not enforce its stated zero-Things and no-lodging premise.
rationale: Assert an empty things array and the exact absent or null lodging shape as separate literal expectations before evaluating the prompt wording.

summary: The mocked reply does not itself satisfy the regression; the test asserts the production gate inputs and prompt facts.
rationale: The script proves first-intake flags would reject the reply, post-intake flags do not, saved title removes titleError, and produceLiveAppReply emits the inviteContactAsk rule. Unexpected fetches return non-OK.

summary: The INV-CLAIM test bypasses the route decision it claims to prove.
rationale: Drive the queue or POST route and assert actual flags, provider calls, HTTP result, and persisted payload.

summary: INV-CLAIM asserts prompt-time ordering and invite behavior.
rationale: It is manifest-wired and fails unless invite-contact facts survive the lodging answer.

summary: The encoded mock host strings dispatch test traffic but do not bypass assertions.
rationale: The joined host constants are test doubles for network routing. The assertions still require the production call path to honor timeout, cap, and stage-budget behavior, and this test result is not substituted for staging evidence.

summary: No observed deployment response proves the claimed Vercel header precedence.
rationale: Capture the final X-Frame-Options header from an allowed deployed keepsake-order response and a non-order control response. Until that evidence exists, do not count this simulator as platform-precedence proof.

summary: The regression calls production filtering and prompt construction.
rationale: It proves positive inclusion and negative exclusion with literal outputs. The known bad venues are adversarial inputs, and no comment or mock directly sets the acceptance result.

summary: Deterministic double preserves the relevant product chain.
rationale: Assertions require one resolved lodging, Kihei-only citations, and no stale lodging geography in the prompt.

summary: The test's comments label executable scenarios; they do not satisfy its assertions.
rationale: The SQL double mutates claims and transcript arrays. The test checks one row and log after sequential and concurrent calls, then verifies a customer reply and a single welcome across trip creation.

summary: The welcome timing test asserts the stored turn count across the actual handler sequence.
rationale: The mock database records four ensureOnboardingOpener calls. Two calls have no trip, then two use the same trip. The final assertions require one stored welcome, a claim and turn bound to that trip, and text equal to renderOnboardingWelcome. The comments label the production sequence but do not satisfy those assertions.

summary: Provider fixtures drive production search and relevance code and include a required rejection case.
rationale: The mock score varies by row, captures the actual area sent to JEV, and throws on unexpected URLs. A prior-only passing row must still make searchPlaces reject with prior_db_sole_source, so fixture data cannot alone manufacture PASS.

summary: The Kihei regression executes production search with positive and negative rows.
rationale: Every judge call must use Kihei, taco survives, gas station is excluded, and chat wrapper status/options are checked.

summary: The test validates observable search behavior.
rationale: It asserts both the provider query and final place list against literal expected behavior. Split host strings affect the test double only and do not make the production result pass.

summary: The chip gate compares rendered behavior and pixels rather than artifact presence alone.
rationale: It checks exact labels, rendered RGB mismatch ratio, container edges, and filter results in a browser. This is adjacent to the #408 LAYOUT-NYC ownership but does not introduce a duplicate issue.

summary: The NYC fixture is regression input; the test measures the current served bundle at both required widths.
rationale: No application code branches on NYC_PR225_SLUG. Failure is based on real browser scroll and checkbox geometry after tab activation. This path does not duplicate the separately owned #408 LAYOUT-NYC verdict work.

summary: The fixed NYC layout path is within #408 ownership; no separate defect is added.
rationale: Keep LAYOUT-NYC follow-through under #408 and do not duplicate it.

summary: The Paia regression rebuilds the production fact flow and asserts the unscheduled contract.
rationale: The test does not pass from its historical comment. It invokes production transformations, parses the generated saved record, forbids the three stale day claims, and requires Paia to remain explicitly not on a day.

summary: The still-blocked rewrite fails closed.
rationale: The successful case returns only the clean model rewrite. Repeating the blocked action claim returns HTTP-equivalent 502, null reply, and reply_unavailable, while preserving diagnostic logging.

summary: The registered test scans relevant served source and generated JS surfaces.
rationale: It scans committed HTML, public JS, rendered Trek output, and dist/assets JS when present. Root dist HTML is not listed, but matching committed HTML inputs are scanned and no build HTML transform injecting these needles was found, so no evidence-backed gap exists.

summary: Served-page layout fails missing measurements and interactions.
rationale: Caught timeouts leave false evidence, absent expected IDs become ok:false, and any false row exits 1. Screenshots are evidence only.

summary: Check I cannot pass from the comments or the HTTP stub alone because the real resolved title must occur in the subject.
rationale: The end-to-end test includes a positive DB fallback and two negative subjects. runShepherdCheckI also requires one outbound row, provider evaluation, accept link, owner name, exact title, and HTTP 200.

summary: The overflow test contains both a clipped pass case and an unclipped fail case.
rationale: The test calls sampleUnclippedHorizontalOverflow for both mock DOM trees. Ancestor clipping suppresses only the Leaflet-like tile, while the 500px element at a 390px viewport must produce a finding. The comments do not affect either result.

summary: The page-eval regression executes the wrapper and verifies both browser consumers use it.
rationale: The test gets 42 from a script built by playwrightEvaluateReturnScript and proves eval rejects a bare top-level return. It then reads the THING-CARD and LAYOUT-NYC consumers, rejects page.evaluate templates containing a bare return, and requires both files to call the wrapper. The preserved comment explains the observed SyntaxError boundary rather than satisfying an assertion.

summary: The regression checks the production prompt boundary.
rationale: Saved lodging remains labelled context and cannot enter citable results. Internal gate rows are removed before model exposure, and literal assertions cover both the system prompt and request body.

owner: TSV #397 follow-through: trip-create critical path regression
summary: The critical-path Nominatim assertion is a hard-coded zero unrelated to HTTP.
rationale: Exercise the real boundary with an instrumented scheduler and prove the response completes before deferred geocoding.

summary: Closed TSV #355 owns the unresolved substitution of synthetic rows for the real trip-level contract.
rationale: Do not file duplicate work. Reopen or supersede TSV #355 and apply the full trip-level contract to sourced PR336 acceptance rows without inventing the missing rows.

summary: The production xAI model id is character-code encoded to evade the hard-coded-content gate.
rationale: Replace the character-code encoding with an explicit reviewed constant or allowlist entry. Remove encoded model reconstruction from recorded fixtures. Extend the evasion scanner and tests to detect String.fromCharCode construction of banned model identifiers.

summary: The runner explicitly limits its verdict to fixture renderability.
rationale: The payload is pinned by bytes and hash, and both positive and negative browser profiles execute. A negative profile passes when it observes a violation, but the script labels that as negative-fixture behavior and never promotes it to Gate B or staging approval.

summary: The side-by-side verifier checks artifact structure and size, not image content.
rationale: #408 replaces #404 and owns LAYOUT-NYC false-pass remediation. Keep this evidence attached to that issue rather than opening a duplicate.

summary: Stale-build proof requires exact full-SHA agreement and fails closed.
rationale: Both operands must be 40 hex characters before strict equality. Version/metadata mismatch throws, and PDF consumers require observed live SHA in both artifacts.

summary: The writer validates committed local assets and does not fetch substitutes.
rationale: Missing or empty JS and CSS throw. The Vite build hook awaits that check, and the hardcoded-content suite rejects reintroducing a travel.timesyncher.com bundle fetch.

summary: Brave normalization has no fixture acceptance path.
rationale: Unusable coordinates and URL identifiers are rejected; no catch returns a passing row.

summary: The intake persistence path merges both live classifier and queued wantedThing shapes without treating either as acceptance evidence.
rationale: intakeThingsForPersistence returns no intake things outside the place-search intake path, and otherwise merges classifier things with job wantedThings. runVacationAppInTurnSearch still requires provider and relevance success before persistence. blockInTurnPlaceReply fails replies that do not cite the resulting in-turn places.

summary: Missing customer-intent keys suppress the safe ask fallback.
rationale: Validate complete response shape, throw on missing/invalid keys, and prove incomplete JSON falls back with ask true.

summary: Email stubs cannot satisfy the smoke send gate.
rationale: Stubbed, failed, pending, and sent remain distinct. Smoke requires sent plus a nonblank provider_message_id, and tests cover stub rejection.

summary: First-intake gap state is derived from customer data and persisted consistently.
rationale: The module does not force a completed intake or successful action. It records lodging presence, invite need, and asked-gap state, then exposes the same structured values to reply facts and transcript payloads.

summary: A failed model reply is synthesized into an ok true Gate B reply.
rationale: Separate user-facing resilience from Gate B evidence. Preserve a fallback response for product availability if desired, but mark fallback use as degraded and make the acceptance gate require a valid model-authored grounded reply. Add tests that fallback responses cannot satisfy Gate B 6/6b.

summary: First-intake lodging persistence is gated and source-backed.
rationale: The path runs only after successful first-intake classification, searches for the stated lodging, deduplicates database rows, and records the lookup result. It does not manufacture a pass when search or persistence is absent.

summary: Category mapping transforms persisted/rendered data but does not decide acceptance.
rationale: Unknown non-lodging categories stay empty or source-labeled rather than becoming a PASS result.

summary: Shared intake fields remain tied to persisted and source records.
rationale: Missing source tags and happy-hour values stay blank. Date assignment, budget values, and presentation overrides all derive from concrete trip or thing data rather than fixture-specific pass synthesis.

summary: The name helper is a production intake filter, not an acceptance override.
rationale: Its broad structural heuristic can admit imperfect proper names, but it does not fabricate a Thing, force a gate pass, or bypass downstream persistence/render checks. The classifier applies it only to model-extracted rows.

summary: Zero or negative env threshold disables Jev filtering.
rationale: Reject unauthorized/out-of-range thresholds; test 0, negative, NaN, and extremes; prove low scores cannot pass any accepted production configuration.

summary: Keepsake overrides copy source-backed content and leave absent content absent.
rationale: It supplies structural category IDs/icons but does not create summary, price, neighborhood, or reviews. PR336 summary padding is owned by #402 elsewhere.

summary: Runtime handler fails on missing token or unsafe style host.
rationale: journeyBookGate is test-only; runtime acceptance is the guarded default handler.

summary: The alternate renderer is quarantined in practice, not only by its comment.
rationale: Repository import search finds renderStyle2Html and buildStyle2Model only in scripts/test_keepsake_style2.mjs. The live keepsake handler builds staging journey URLs and never imports this module, so its fixture HTML cannot stand in for product acceptance.

summary: The module is an offline comparator helper and does not approve the live UI.
rationale: No production staging gate imports it. Its presentation constant and comparisons are exercised by offline tests, while the served UI has a separate sort implementation and smoke evidence.

summary: The cache layer validates payloads and does not turn an invalid geocode into success.
rationale: Higher-limit alias reuse is permitted only when the cached limit meets the request and the payload passes cacheability checks. Invalid payloads miss or throw through the caller rather than becoming synthetic place rows.

summary: The parser fail-closes malformed scores while retaining an intentional legacy shape.
rationale: choice/value precede type:score, but existing production fixtures and eval inputs use untyped choice. Bounded integer checks reject arbitrary truthy values, and malformed scores throw. No governing contract was found that forbids compatibility input.

summary: Invalid budgets and exhaustion fail closed.
rationale: Caller omits unscored rows and propagates typed timeout errors.

summary: Anchors remain source-derived and separately scoped.
rationale: No fixture geography or PASS synthesis is present.

summary: Missing/unknown place-search categories return errors.
rationale: Empty enum value is limited to non-place_search turns.

summary: Nominatim failures degrade with explicit diagnostics, not success labels.
rationale: Wrong hosts, non-OK responses, and invalid JSON throw. tryGeocodeLabel returns null for fallback but records error/empty/skipped status and reason.

summary: Selection returns one judged winner or no ambiguous save.
rationale: Upstream relevance omits unjudged rows.

summary: OSM category assignment is structural and unsupported tags stay empty.
rationale: The table does not inspect names or fixture IDs. Production filters requested categories and maps provider tags through the same rules, preventing name-based canned acceptance.

summary: The OSM structural gate rejects generic infrastructure before persistence.
rationale: A record needs a name and a recognized POI root tag. Highway, junction, crossing, slipway, and generic bridge, entrance, or access records fail unless they also carry a business POI tag. Tests include literal failing road/access examples and a passing market before the normal mapper and radius filter run.

summary: Provider summaries reject errors and do not call an absent log empty.
rationale: All-empty requires recognized rows, rejects any error/hit, and permits skipped only in a known provider set. Production reaches it after prior and Brave stages provide answered evidence.

summary: The center helper applies its stated precedence in the provider path without a skip branch.
rationale: Named-place lookups use the context destination center while explicit anchor geocodes take priority for anchored searches. A lodging-marked context center remains selected before the generic stored destination fallback. The caller uses the returned center for provider filtering and does not convert a missing center into pass evidence.

summary: Successful classifications missing turnKind fail the contract.
rationale: The helper returns a specific error when ok is true but turnKind is not recognized. Unknown values do not default to a passing category.

summary: Provider secret names are deliberately split and suffix-matched, while the deploy scanner contains a bespoke decoder for that exact split.
rationale: Replace suffix discovery and joined key-name fragments with an explicit boundary mapping that the repository's policy permits and scans normally. Remove the scanner's syntax-specific decoder. Add negative coverage for similarly suffixed decoy variables and prove only the intended provider keys are read. Coordinate any policy exception explicitly rather than encoding around the rule.

summary: Only provider rows surviving rejection, source, venue, and radius rules become citable.
rationale: Saved itinerary and prior-db titles are moved to notCitableAsResult, internal allow lists are hidden from the model, and final reply shipping rechecks unsourced mentions. The grounded fallback can name only citablePlaceTitles and fails when none exist.

summary: Event logo enrichment enforces official-site attribution.
rationale: A logo is accepted only when its hostname matches the attributed website. Missing evidence is marked, and shared output can explicitly fail duplicate unrelated logos.

summary: The VK contract accepts an empty batch and 15 unsupported-category rows.
rationale: Fail empty lists, reject unsupported categories before counting, and add literal expected-failure tests.

summary: The split budget-key literal is already owned by #403.
rationale: Do not duplicate the contract's existing budget-key string-splitting finding.

summary: The API budget synchronizer derives exposed amounts from persisted prices and saved targets.
rationale: The handler promotes metadata targets before list finalization. syncSharedTripApiBudget rebuilds lines from shared rows and the promoted target map, while budgetGateAllowedAmounts uses the same served payload the live tab receives. The split bucket label is owned by TSV #403 and is not duplicated here.

summary: Base copies source fields; PR336 adds known padding risk.
rationale: Do not duplicate PR336 summary-padding ownership.

summary: Patch markers feed the existing LAYOUT-NYC acceptance path owned by TSV #408.
rationale: Do not open a duplicate LAYOUT-NYC finding for these marker patches.

summary: The boundary delegates to production payload preparation without fixture padding.
rationale: No path, slug, NYC identity, or acceptance flag changes the result. PR336 React receives the same prepared shape as API and tests, so this wrapper does not synthesize missing fields.

summary: Customer-only stubs remain incomplete, while search-enriched things carry provider detail into the completeness gate.
rationale: shouldApplyAutoDetailFields requires explicit detail, a recognized provider, or substantive sourceRecord fields. missingDetailFieldsForCategory checks category-specific fields, four sourced reviews where applicable, coordinates, summary sources, and description/summary length; comments are not data and do not satisfy it.

summary: A bare matching brand name can manufacture a favicon and hide a future logo-source gap.
rationale: Require persisted logo, favicon, website, or source-record evidence before deriving a brand favicon. Keep the current sourced Priceline row, add a negative bare-name case, and render the category glyph with logoCaptureReason when no sourced logo exists.

summary: Synthetic proof images are explicit fixtures and do not determine visual acceptance.
rationale: proofPngBuffer runs only for the bind CLI --proof option and unit/storage checks. Print/share filters remove proof rows, and the staging bind-media smoke uses a separate one-pixel payload to test storage/cache semantics rather than screenshot quality. No visual gate treats either image as product-media evidence.

summary: Patch removes expense defaults and critical misses throw.
rationale: Known #403 key splitting is elsewhere; this module uses the persisted key directly.

summary: Served map patch fails on missing markers/order/Leaflet.
rationale: Known #408 judge ownership is outside this patch.

summary: Constant is static-print-only and has no verdict.
rationale: Consumer retains live Leaflet/OSM checks.

summary: Assertions inspect served output, not patch constants.
rationale: Handler checks the built asset and rejects hardcoded geography, fixture coordinates, canned copy, placeholders, missed patches, and missing media. #408 judge path is separate.

summary: The classifier merge preserves both extraction and queued wantedThing inputs without manufacturing success.
rationale: mergeWantedThings deduplicates cleaned classifier and fallback records. classifyTripIntake still requires successful decision and extraction responses, validates required dates when configured, and returns explicit failure data otherwise. Queue and chat callers consume the merged records as search work, not as accepted places.

summary: The map hook publishes observed Leaflet state and does not detect capture or modify map behavior.
rationale: It returns false only when no map container exists, otherwise reads the live center, zoom, and bounds on initial bind and map events. No fixture, screenshot, or acceptance result is synthesized.

summary: Map initialization returns an explicit unresolved failure when evidence is absent.
rationale: The function prefers actual place points, uses stored destination coordinates only as a declared fallback, and returns ok false with map_center_unresolved when neither exists. The browser bundle receives the same function body.

summary: Logo persistence records success or a miss reason without treating a miss as a logo.
rationale: logoUrl is written only when capture succeeds. logoCaptureReason remains diagnostic. PR336 changes capture rules but leaves this adapter unchanged.

summary: Content tags are model-backed and failures remain explicit.
rationale: Deterministic logic adds only speaker, direction, voice, and supplied payload tags. Customer-word content tags come from the model, and a model failure returns ask:true with an error rather than a confident inferred tag set.

summary: Provenance exemptions require explicit blocker evidence.
rationale: Blocked fields are ignored unless blocker text is nonempty. Alias claims require matching title, ccab key, and evidence URL. Hotel coordinates stay required unless blocked, and row 608 remains intentionally failing.

summary: assert_can_edit trusts two matching client-controlled values.
rationale: Remove raw equality or authenticate it at a trusted boundary; derive owner from the trip; add HTTP negative proof that forged matching body/header values receive 403.

summary: Wind fallback returns observed readings and cannot invent acceptance copy.
rationale: Provider errors and timeout degrade to an empty optional forecast. The module composes no swim note or fixture answer and caches only nonempty observed readings.
